issues.description: The solution's ExcellenceLand class declares isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck) (i.e., a boolean getter that takes a parameter), while the problem statement requires adding public getters for all attributes (no-argument getters). This creates a signature mismatch for the expected getter of the excellentEnough attribute and will confuse students or cause tests to fail which expect a no-argument boolean getter (e.g., isExcellentEnough()).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's ExcellenceLand method signature to a no-argument getter: public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; } so it matches the problem requirement to provide public getters for all attributes (and follows the standard boolean getter naming convention).

issues.description: The problem statement requires public getters for all attributes (no parameters). In the solution, the boolean attribute 'excellentEnough' has a getter declared as isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck) (takes a parameter) instead of a parameterless getter (e.g., isExcellentEnough()). This signature mismatch conflicts with the stated requirement and will confuse students mapping the specification to the implementation and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution method to a standard parameterless getter: public boolean isExcellentEnough() (or public boolean getExcellentEnough()) so it matches the problem statement's requirement for public getters with no parameters.
